text: In the twenty-second chapter of Genesis a question is raised which is never answered. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, whom he loves; and of what he feels the narrator tells us nothing, never once looking within him. Upon Abraham's silence the whole chapter turns, and he has rather the aspect of a silence than of a character. He makes no protest and offers no bargain; there is nothing left in him of the man who pleaded for Sodom.
